_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The Green River Valley Water Treatment Plant is a non-responding facility.  If any release occurs, the operators will evacuate and report to the appropriate response point.  The facility, if invited will participate in field and/or tabletop exercises with Kentucky and/or Hart Co Emergency Management and/or local area responders. 

Depending on wind direction and severity of the emergency, facility response points will consist of two potential predetermined locations.  The primary location (south end) will be the old Rodgers Store in Canmer, north of Hwy 677 and 31E.  The secondary location (north end) will be at Green River Hill Grocery on Hwy 31E.  The response points were determined with the wind direction from the southwest to the northeast.  An immediate assessment needs to be made of wind direction and modifications to this plan will be made at the time of each individual release event.

The Facility Representative(s) who meets the emergency response personnel shall have a copy of the Process Safety Management / Risk Management Plan, the EPCRA Tier II Report, and SDS sheets and should brief the responders on the current situation.  The distance to the endpoint (worst case release scenario) the substance could travel 2.2 miles before dispersing enough to no longer pose a hazard to the public.

Citizens will be advised of the situation and provided instruction from the Kentucky and/or Hart Co Emergency Management and/or local area responders through emergency service public address systems.

As required by 40 CFR 68, Subpart E, Green River Valley Water District will submit annual EPCRA Tier II Reports and comply with any other actions specified by the Hart Co. LEPC to fulfill the requirement to ensure that the facility is incorporated into the community emergency response plan and that the local response organizations are aware of the storage of chlorine at the facility.  Additionally, the annual notification exercise will be conducted. 

Green River Valley Water

District management attend annual meetings with Hart County, Ky officials, often including the Hart Co Emergency Manager, where the subject of chlorine storage at the facility is routinely discussed.  With the 2021 relocation of chlorine storage to a new building, the Hart Co Emergency Management was provided an on-site tour to observe the new storage building, the new overall facility layout, and identify new facility access points and topography.

Employees receive initial and subsequent training on the dangers of chlorine, process safety and risk management, and standard chlorine process equipment operating procedures.  Employees also have monthly safety meetings regarding chemical safety and procedures for the proper use of the chlorine process equipment.  Emergency equipment is on hand only for aiding GRVWD employees in the safe evacuation of the release location.  The emergency equipment includes, 30-minute Scott Air-Pak breathing apparatus, rubber boots, gloves, face shields, and splash proof safety goggles.  The facility intends to add cartridge type escape respirators to their inventory.  The interior atmosphere of the chlorine storage building is continually monitored for the presence of chlorine vapors and the chlorine cylinder and connected processing equipment are routinely manually checked for leaks.

Chlorine is transported by truck on I-65 and US 31E into Canmer to the water treatment plant by Water Solutions Unlimited, 8824 Union Mills Dr., Camby, IN 46113, (800) 359-3570.  Cylinders are unloaded by boom.  Hazardous areas include Munfordville, Hardyville and Canmer, KY.  A maximum of six (6) 1-ton cylinders, approximately 12,000 lbs., are handled and stored.

With any accidental release, if the door to the facility can be closed safely and the ventilation shut off, a minor release may partially be contained in the chlorine room.  One remedial measure the community responders can employ to reduce the impact of a release would include a water spray d

irected at the vapors, not the point of leak, to reduce vapors.  The water spray runoff can be contained and neutralized with soda ash.  The Hart Co. LEPC would be contacted to oversee the spill containment, cleanup and disposal to ensure all is accomplished per EPA and KY Dept. of Natural Resources regulations.  The primary hazardous material clean-up contractor will be Clean Earth, 1877-577-2669.  If not available, Chemtrec would be called to activate Chlorep (Chlorine Emergency Response Team) to clean up spill.  Any cleanup of hazardous waste will be accomplished through a plan approved by KY Natural Resources and/or US EPA. 

The Green River Valley Water District has not had any chlorine release in the past 5 years.

During the 2025 Process Hazard Analysis and the 2025 Compliance Audit, a number of recommendations were made to decrease the likely hood that a release could occur and reduce the likely hood of operator exposure.  The changes resulting from the recommendations will improve the safety of the chlorine process and provide further protection of the operators.
